newsitem.title: GERMANY: EU gene label decision neutral for Nestle Germany.
newsitem.headline: EU gene label decision neutral for Nestle Germany.

text.p: A European Union decision to bring genetically modified soya and maize under the EU novel food law had no impact on Nestle food labelling and marketing in Germany, a spokesman for Nestle Deutschland AG said.
The EU earlier today said it was assessing which products from the two categories must be labelled by November 1.
Nestle Deutschland was complying with the novel food law which came into effect in May and lays down rules for new foods' safety, he said.

Products using derivatives from foods that were genetically modified and significantly different from conventional products would be labelled, as was mandatory, along Dutch labelling models, but this was currently not the case.
"Such products would be the exception to the rule in the long term," the spokesman said.
Nestle laboratories could vouch for the best possible analysis of raw materials and derived products to determine whether genetic modification could still be traced, he added.
In the Netherlands, food products made from genetically modified soybeans have been labelled since April, making the country the first in Europe to take a unilateral stand.
Nestle in 1996 had food sales worth 7.4 billion marks in Germany.
Bonn-based national food industry institute BLL, which supplies scientific and legal services across the industry, was not immediately available for comment.
